name: Mercury
description: The smallest and innermost planet, a scorched, cratered world with almost no atmosphere and the most extreme temperature swings in the Solar System.
funFact: A day on Mercury (sunrise to sunrise) lasts about 176 Earth days — longer than its entire year.

name: Venus
description: Earth's near-twin in size, shrouded in a thick, toxic atmosphere of carbon dioxide that traps heat and makes it the hottest planet in the Solar System.
funFact: Venus spins backwards compared to most planets, so the Sun rises in the west and sets in the east.

name: Earth
description: Our home world, the only known planet with liquid water on its surface, a breathable atmosphere, and life.
funFact: Earth is the only planet not named after a Greek or Roman god.

name: Mars
description: The 'Red Planet,' colored by iron oxide (rust) on its surface, home to the largest volcano and canyon in the Solar System.
funFact: Mars hosts Olympus Mons, a volcano nearly three times the height of Mount Everest.

name: Jupiter
description: The largest planet in the Solar System, a swirling giant of hydrogen and helium famous for its Great Red Spot, a storm that has raged for centuries.
funFact: Jupiter is so massive that its gravity helps shield the inner Solar System from many comets and asteroids.

name: Saturn
description: Famous for its spectacular ring system made of ice and rock, Saturn is the least dense planet in the Solar System — it would float in water.
funFact: Saturn's rings are made almost entirely of water ice, with particles ranging from dust-sized to house-sized.

name: Uranus
description: A pale blue-green ice giant that rotates on its side, likely the result of an ancient collision, giving it the most extreme seasons in the Solar System.
funFact: Uranus's axis is tilted about 98 degrees, so it essentially spins on its side as it orbits the Sun.

name: Neptune
description: The most distant planet from the Sun, a deep blue ice giant with the fastest winds in the Solar System, reaching over 2,000 km/h.
funFact: Neptune was the first planet located through mathematical prediction rather than direct observation.
